This article details his struggles and triumphs, culminating in his short yet impactful stint with the Los Angeles Angels.
articles.body: Trey Mancini’s return to MLB was a much longer and more complex process than a typical comeback. The former Baltimore Orioles standout had not been in the majors since July 31, 2023, and spent the next years navigating minor-league opportunities, releases and uncertainty as to whether another MLB opportunity would come. The Los Angeles Angels selected his contract on June 8, 2026, and Mancini finally got to the goal he kept pursuing.The return was 1,043 days after his last major league appearance, and it was especially meaningful because retirement had been a real possibility several times. Mancini’s had one major comeback in his career after he missed the 2020 season while being treated for Stage 3 colon cancer. His return to the Angels was another try to extend a career that had been interrupted multiple times by circumstances beyond his control.Trey Mancini completes remarkable MLB return with Los Angeles AngelsMancini signed a minor league deal with the Angels to start the 2026 season after spending last season at Triple-A in the Arizona Diamondbacks organization. His MLB opportunity came on the heels of a solid run with Triple-A Salt Lake, where his experience and offensive production helped put him back on the major league radar.Then Mancini’s wait was over when the Angels took his contract on June 8. He was immediately slotted into the lineup against the Houston Astros, a team he used to play for and a team he won a World Series with in 2022.Mancini didn’t just see this as another game but recognized the importance of coming back after such a long absence. He made an immediate impact in his first game, going 3-for-4 with an RBI and one run.But the performance gave Mancini the kind of start that could have opened another chapter in his big league career. He’d spent months grinding through the minors, waiting for another chance to show he could still play at the highest level.Mancini’s five-game Angels stint ultimately produced a line of 4-for-13, including a triple and four RBIs. He was outrighted to Triple-A on June 17 and was designated for assignment by the Angels, who he elected free agency.2026 Angels comebackDetailsMLB returnJune 8, 2026Days away from MLB1,043Previous MLB appearanceJuly 31, 2023TeamLos Angeles AngelsGames played5Batting average0.308Hits4RBIs4Triple1Trey Mancini overcame setbacks before major league returnThe road to Anaheim had plenty of points in which Mancini wondered if it was realistic to keep playing. He departed the Chicago Cubs organization in 2023 and had a few minor league chances but did not return to MLB.Mancini’s next stop after the Cubs was the Cincinnati Reds, but he never reached the majors. He signed with the Miami Marlins organization in 2024 and was released before the season started. He got another shot with the Arizona Diamondbacks in 2025, but he spent the entire season in Triple-A Reno.Retirement became a real consideration during that period. Mancini had considered retiring from playing at least three times in the three years leading up to his return, MLB.com reported.The tie-in became all the more meaningful when the Angels hired Anderson as their hitting coach for 2026. Mancini then inked a minor-league deal with Los Angeles, giving the veteran another route to the majors.It took patience to get the chance. Instead of jumping straight to the Angels, Mancini began the year with Triple-A Salt Lake. He kept putting up numbers in the minors until the stars aligned and his numbers ignited an opportunity on the big league roster.Trey Mancini’s comeback adds another chapter to careerMancini already had one of baseball’s best-known comeback stories to his credit. A product of the 2013 MLB Draft, when the Orioles selected him in the eighth round, he reached the Major Leagues in 2016.He was a productive middle-of-the-order presence in Baltimore, peaking statistically in 2019. That year, Mancini batted.291 with 35 home runs and 97 RBIs, career highs in both categories.Then, his career was interrupted significantly when he was diagnosed with Stage 3 colon cancer in 2020. Mancini missed the entire season undergoing treatment and surgery before returning to the Orioles in 2021.His return earned him American League Comeback Player of the Year honors. He went deep 21 times and drove in 71 runs in 147 games, providing one of the best examples of his ability to recover from a major setback.Mancini was later traded by the Baltimore to the Astros in 2022 and was part of Houston’s World Series championship club. The ceremony was held at Camden Yards on Sept. 19, offering one final link to the organization that drafted him and where he spent most of his career.Trey Mancini returns to MLB with AngelsSo Mancini’s final chapter in MLB had a different meaning than your typical comeback story. articles.title: New MLB Rumors on Reds Exec's Frustration After 'Laundry List' of Nixed Trades by Owner
articles.summary: As the Cincinnati Reds put the finishing touches on another season without reaching the playoffs, frustration appears to be growing in the front office between ownership and president of baseball operations Nick Krall.
articles.body:
As the Cincinnati Reds put the finishing touches on another season without reaching the playoffs, frustration appears to be growing in the front office between ownership and president of baseball operations Nick Krall.

Per The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and C. Trent Rosencrans , Krall pushed back at Reds owner Bob Castellini during a meeting earlier in the season with a "laundry list" of potential trades he could have executed that were nixed by Castellini.

The report noted Krall's list came out in response to Castellini asking "why aren't we the Brewers?"

Vladdy Defends Quote About $500M Deal 🌶️

Castellini's question was in regards to the divide in the standings and sustained success by the Milwaukee Brewers when they, like the Reds, operate with a payroll that regularly ranks in the bottom half of MLB.

Specific trades that got nixed were not cited in the story, but it was noted Castellini "has consistently balked" when Krall has attempted to implement a plan centered around building a strong core of young talent and enhancing the group by trading "established players at peak value when they are still affordable and under club control."

It's a formula some of the most consistently successful small market teams have followed for years. The Brewers, Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians are among the lowest-spending teams in MLB, but all three teams have made the playoffs at least five times since 2018.

The Guardians and Rays have both played in the World Series once since 2016. Milwaukee has reached the NLCS twice since the 2018 season.

By comparison, the Reds have made the playoffs five times since 1996. Their last playoff series win was over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the 1995 NLDS.

Castellini's tenure doesn't cover that entire period since he didn't buy the Reds until January 2006 , but no one would describe this 20-year period as a success for the franchise.

Phil Castellini, Bob's son, took over control of the franchise in February as part of a planned succession plan since his father turned 85 on Wednesday.

Reds fans remember Phil as the one who had to apologize in April 2022 after a radio interview in which he replied to a question about why fans should be optimistic for the franchise by saying "where are you going to go?"

The Reds' .476 winning percentage since the start of the 2006 season is tied with the Washington Nationals for the seventh-worst in MLB. The Nationals can fall back on having a World Series title in 2019.

For a franchise that's not spending big money at the MLB level to win, the farm system hasn't been robust in recent years.

Per MLB.com , the Reds have only had a top-10 farm system once in five rankings dating back to the 2024 midseason update. The 2026 in-season update had their prospect pool ranked No. 23 with Alfredo Duno and Steele Hall as their only top-100 prospects.

Going back to the more successful small-market clubs, the farm systems for theRays and Brewers ranked second and third, respectively. Cleveland fell to No. 12 primarily because Travis Bazzana, Chase DeLauter and Parker Messick all graduated.

The Reds' system has produced some star-level talent in recent years, including Elly De La Cruz, Sal Stewart and Chase Burns. Hunter Greene would also make that list, but he had elbow surgery in August that has left his status for 2027 unclear.

Their problem, though, has been their inability to supplement the talent around that group. Burns is their only pitcher with at least 20 starts who has an ERA under 4.61.

Cincinnati's lineup ranks fourth in MLB with 208 home runs, but last with a .305 on-base percentage.

The Reds' 73-85 record is the worst in the NL Central. This will be their first time finishing last in the division since 2018.

articles.title: Bold Predictions for the Final Games of the MLB Season
articles.summary: This morning felt different. I stepped outside and felt a slight chill in the air, and even thought about throwing on a sweatshirt. My car’s engine took an e...
articles.body:
I stepped outside and felt a slight chill in the air, and even thought about throwing on a sweatshirt. My car's engine took an extra rev to start. I stepped on a dried-up leaf on the sidewalk, and it satisfactorily crunched and cracked beneath my shoe. That's when I knew: playoff baseball was here.

There is under a week left in the 2026 regular season of Major League Baseball. Of the four Wild Card series starting on Tuesday, just one matchup is set. That leaves so much to be settled in so few games. So much so that anything can happen.

Here are the boldest predictions and possible outcomes in the homestretch of one of the most unique seasons in baseball history.

The San Diego Padres Will Host a Wild Card series

At the All-Star break, the San Diego Padres were an even 48-48. But somehow, that record felt generous for how the Padres were playing. At the time, San Diego had the third-worst offense in wRC+ and was dead last in runs.

One of the most exciting and energizing teams in the league had seemingly lost their edge. The Padres were in 10th place in the National League and 5.5 games behind the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies , who held the top two Wild Card spots all year.

Then something clicked. The lineup explosively turned around, primarily led by $340 million outfielder Fernando Tatis Jr. At the All-Star break, Tatis Jr. had five home runs. Since then, he's hit 20 bombs in 59 games while slashing a .292 average, .371 OBP and blazing .601 SLG.

The wins slowly started to add up, but it wasn't until September that the Padres ignited. San Diego's gone on eight and five game win streaks and has won 14 of its last 16 games. This stretch effectively ended the Wild Card race and has even propelled them above the Cubs and Phillies by one game.

This means the final games between the three determine who plays who, or more importantly, who hosts who in next week's Wild Card series. The team that finishes last out of the trio will face the Atlanta Braves , who clinched the NL East on Sunday. The first-place team will host the second-place team in the three-game series.

The idea of the Padres hosting a Wild Card series was unfathomable just weeks ago. But this run will enter San Diego as the hottest team in October, able to stack up against anyone.

The Chicago White Sox Will Take the AL Central

The darling Chicago White Sox have unpredictably led the AL Central for the majority of the season. Chicago's been the best story of 2026, with that story far from over.

The White Sox opened September 3-7 and gave up the lead in the division to the Cleveland Guardians last Wednesday. Chicago was in first since July 22.

Late-season comebacks are something Cleveland is accustomed to. Just last year, the Guardians unbelievably erased an 11-game deficit against the Detroit Tigers in 20 days. The Guardians went on to win the division but lost to Detroit in the Wild Card series.

Thankfully for Chicago, the Colorado Rockies come into town for the final series of the regular season. The Guardians wrap up a series against the playoff-prepped Boston Red Sox , then travel to play their final three games against the Kansas City Royals . The Royals record doesn't blow the Rockies out of the water, but since the break, Kansas City's gone 29-31.

Another blessing for Chicago is that they just need to tie Cleveland at the end of the season. The White Sox clinched the tiebreaker over the Guardians on Sept. 14 amid their release of first place.

Winning the AL Central doesn't just give Midwest bragging rights and another banner; it'll deliver a playoff bye. The poor state of the AL West confirms that whoever comes out on top will host an AL Division Series. With how the bracket's shaping up, a White Sox-Guardians best-of-five ALDS seems imminent.

However, as of Sept. 23, the White Sox trail by one game with four to play. The South Siders will have to handle the Rockies, then cheer on their division-rival Royals. Cleveland has been playing winning baseball through September, but the art of the "spoiler" never fails to ingrain.

The Houston Astros Will Become the Worst Division Winner in MLB History

The worst division winner in MLB history belongs to the 2005 Padres, who won the NL West at 82-80. With four games to play, the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are tied for first in the AL West at 78-80.

Not only will the Padres' record likely be broken, but baseball could see its first sub-.500 division winner. The Astros visit the abysmal Athletics for their final four games, and the Rangers visit the less-abysmal Minnesota Twins .

Texas had a golden opportunity to close out the West this week, hosting the truly abysmal New York Mets . The Rangers lost that series and gave up a one-game lead while doing so.

The not-so-brutal, honest truth is that neither of these clubs deserves to win a division. The fanbases would say so themselves. In another world, both the Rangers' and Astros' seasons would be over by August and focused on next year. Instead, two games below .500 entering the final weekend, they're in a heated division race with playoffs at stake.

The bracket format would pit whoever wins the mild, mild West against the loser of the Central. No matter White Sox-Guardians or Rangers-Astros, the Central's representative will be favored. That said, winning the West will either give Houston or Texas home-field advantage in that best-of-three. This season, the Rangers have the fourth-most home wins in the AL, compared to the Astros' 11th-most.

If the season ended in today's tie, the Astros would win via the tiebreaker. It'd be Houston's eighth AL West title in the last decade.

This isn't a battle of the best team; it's a thrilling battle of who's worse.

In true 2026 season fashion, it all comes down to the final weekend. With the real fun around the corner, baseball fans can just sit back and enjoy.

articles.title: The decision that changed Bryce Harper’s career and shaped his journey from teenage baseball prodigy to MLB superstar and two-time MVP
articles.summary: Explore how Bryce Harper's decision to leave high school early for junior college baseball transformed him into an MLB superstar and two-time MVP.
articles.body: Bryce Harper’s road to MLB was different from most teenage prospects. Now an unbelievable amateur talent in Las Vegas, Harper opted to fast-track his education and baseball timeline rather than stay in high school through graduation. The move put him in junior college baseball, and he was younger than most of the players around him.The decision opened a door few prospects get. Harper earned his GED and enrolled at the College of Southern Nevada, making him eligible for the 2010 MLB Draft at age 17. His performance against older competition quickly made the gamble a defining stage of his development, eventually leading the Washington Nationals to take him with the No. 1 overall pick.What was Bryce Harper’s bold early move that shaped MLB career?Harper’s turning point came when he was still in high school in Las Vegas. He didn’t go the traditional high school route, but earned his GED after his sophomore year and enrolled at the College of Southern Nevada. The move was intended to accelerate his eligibility for the MLB Draft.The decision was important because Harper was getting extraordinary attention even before he entered professional baseball. He appeared on the cover of Sports Illustrated at age 16, a sign of the expectations that surrounded him. Thus, the early move only served to bring more attention to a teenager who was already being groomed as a potential future MLB star.The College of Southern Nevada gave Harper something that high school did not: the chance to play against older players and get ready for the 2010 Draft. MLB records show he was just 17 years old during his junior college season, although he was the age of a high school junior.Still, the move did not guarantee immediate success. Harper stepped into a new world with big expectations and had to adjust to playing against college players. The pressure was pretty high around him for a junior college athlete, with scouts and media watching him like a hawk during his performances.His reply came by way of production. Harper batted .443 with 31 home runs and 98 RBIs in 66 games for the College of Southern Nevada in 2010. When the 2010 MLB Draft arrived, the Washington Nationals picked him first overall.The Nationals then signed the 17-year-old to a five-year, $9.9 million deal with a $6.25 million signing bonus, according to MLB’s career timeline. The pick achieved the short-term goal of the unconventional educational and baseball choice Harper had made years earlier.Harper’s progression from junior college to the pros was also rapid. He reached the Majors in 2012 at age 19, was an All-Star and won National League Rookie of the Year. That early acceleration had propelled him from high school prospect to MLB player in a remarkably short period.Bryce Harper turned teenage pressure into successThe expectations had been building since Harper was a teenager, and the No. 1 overall pick carried them. At age 22, he batted .330 with a .460 on-base percentage and .649 slugging percentage, hit 42 home runs and won his first National League MVP Award. MLB says he is the youngest player to ever win the award unanimously.Bryce Harper built a legacy beyond expectationsAfter moving to Philadelphia, Harper’s career continued to evolve. In 2021, he posted a 1.044 OPS, 42 doubles and 35 home runs in 141 games, earning his second National League MVP Award.That second MVP cemented the bridge from his teenage rep to his long-term MLB achievements. Instead of just being a very good No. 1 pick, Harper developed into a guy who piled up major individual awards at different points in his career.His postseason performances for the Phillies have also become a big part of his career narrative. Harper homered in the game-winning run in Game 5 of the National League Championship Series and was named the NLCS MVP in 2022 before making his World Series debut.Harper was on the active roster of the Phillies through the 2026 season, adding to his statistical record. articles.body:
Welcome to the history books, Pete Crow-Armstrong.

The soon-to-be National League MVP became the first Chicago Cubs player and seventh player of all time to hit 40 home runs and steal 40 bases in a single season on Thursday. He walked in his first at-bat and wasted no time, stealing his 40th base of the year on the very next pitch:

Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000 🏆

How Cubs Broke 108-Year World Series Curse 🤯

Crow-Armstrong joined one of the most exclusive lists in baseball history that is populated by some of the all-time legends of the game.

Jose Canseco became the first to reach the 40/40 club but was later joined by icons such as Barry Bonds and Shohei Ohtani in the following years. It is also something that has happened more recently of late, as the Cubs center fielder became the third player to do so in the last four years.

Atlanta Braves star Ronald Acuña Jr. did so in 2023 before Ohtani accomplished as much in 2024.

As for Crow-Armstrong, he's a primary reason the Cubs are in playoff position despite so many injuries to their pitching staff. With 45 homers, he is the only player on the team to reach the 30 mark. And with 40 steals, he is the only Cub with more than 22 swiped bags.

He has led the way for an offense that is first in the league in runs scored but is also arguably the best defensive player in the league.

In fact, Crow-Armstrong has a fielding run value of 27, per Baseball Savant , which is the best mark in baseball. St. Louis Cardinals shortstop Wetherholt is the only other player in the league at better than 17 with a total of 23.

Chicago's postseason potential will likely come down to whether the pitching staff can exceed expectations in the face of so many injuries to Cade Horton, Justin Steele and Ben Brown, among others.

But as long as Crow-Armstrong is in the lineup, the team has an opportunity to defeat any opponent with his combination of power, speed and fielding.

If nothing else, he will be taking home the National League MVP as a result of his incredible season.

Things weren't much better in 2025 as the White Sox finished 60-102, marking their third consecutive year with at least 100 losses. They have already set a new record for most wins by a team coming off at least three straight 100-loss seasons.

articles.title: White Sox SS Colson Montgomery ties MLB single-season strikeout record that has stood for 17 years
articles.summary: Montgomery notched his 223rd strikeout of the season on Thursday, tying a record set in 2009 by Mark Reynolds.
articles.body:
On Thursday, as the White Sox clinched their first playoff berth in five seasons , the Chicago shortstop made a little bit of history with one of MLB's least-desired records.

With a strikeout in the White Sox's 9-1 win over the Kansas City Royals , Colson Montgomery tied MLB's record for the most strikeouts in a single season — a record that had stood for 17 years. Montgomery now has 223 strikeouts this season, with three games remaining before Chicago heads to the postseason.

Montgomery struck out in the third inning of Thursday's game, with reliever Anthony Gose dispatching him during his third at-bat after the White Sox got off to a hot start. The 24-year-old shortstop went 0-4, flying out three times in addition to his historic strikeout.

Luisangel Acuña pinch hit for Montgomery in his final at-bat in the ninth, temporarily ending Montgomery's chances of breaking the dubious mark.

The original record, set by former Arizona Diamondbacks infielder Mark Reynolds in 2009, seemed likely to be broken this season thanks to a surge of high-strikeout hitters. Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber is just five strikeouts behind the mark, while Los Angeles Angels shortstop Zach Neto is at 209 strikeouts.

But Montgomery has surged ahead to tie the strikeout title in a sort of come-from-behind win, thanks in part to a late cluster of strikeouts over the last few months. In September alone, Montgomery has had seven games with at least three strikeouts. He has six four-strikeout games stretching across the season.

Even with the high number of strikeouts, Montgomery's hitting hasn't been completely atrocious: Though his batting average (.202) and on-base percentage (.288) have been low, his slugging percentage (.418) and OPS (.701) are near-league average. He has 31 home runs, 112 hits and 87 RBIs.

Multiple players have come close to Reynolds' record over the years, but none have matched the former infielder's mark before this season. Reynolds told The Athletic in July that he used to see the stat as "embarrassing," but now views it as a "badge of honor."

"Now, I'm older. Have perspective. People ask me, 'Do you want someone to break it?' I'm like, 'No. How many big-league records do you have?'" Reynolds said at the time.

In the same interview, Reynolds joked that he might have to hand off the strikeout honor to whoever breaks the record on "SportsCenter." But there's still a nonzero chance that multiple players will pass him, with Schwarber coming around the corner with four games remaining.

For now, though, Montgomery can claim sole ownership of a place in the record books, for better or for worse.

articles.summary: It has been a roller-coaster season of injuries, winning streaks, losing streaks, poor pitching and an MVP performance, but the Chicago Cubs are going to the playoffs for the second straight year.
articles.body:
It has been a roller-coaster season of injuries, winning streaks, losing streaks, poor pitching and an MVP performance, but the Chicago Cubs are going to the playoffs for the second straight year.

Chicago clinched its postseason spot with a 2-1 win over the Miami Marlins on Thursday, which came just minutes after the Chicago White Sox also clinched a spot.

***Indicates clinched division and first-round bye

The Cubs had high expectations heading into the season after reaching the playoffs in 2025 and then adding Alex Bregman to an already potent lineup in the offseason, but the path to the postseason was anything but smooth.

Perhaps becoming the second team in MLB history to record two 10-game winning streaks and a 10-game losing streak in the same season—and doing so by May—should have been a sign of the uneven path.

Presumed ace Cade Horton was lost for the season to Tommy John surgery in April, which was an even more difficult blow because top-line starter Justin Steele missed most of last year and this year with his own Tommy John surgery. The idea of Steele potentially returning in 2026 didn't fully come into the picture until he made rehab appearances in September.

Those were far from the only pitching injuries, as Matthew Boyd, Edward Cabrera and Ben Brown all spent significant time on the injured list. Brown was lost for the season because of a rehab setback , which was a difficult break since he had emerged as one of the team's best pitchers when others were sidelined.

Injuries were not limited to the starting staff, as the bullpen saw Daniel Palencia, Phil Maton, Riley Martin, Hunter Harvey and Porter Hodge, among others, all deal with setbacks.

The end result has been arguably the worst pitching staff in baseball, although the front office did bolster it some with the additions of Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes ahead of the trade deadline.

Despite the pitching, Chicago is still heading to the postseason in large part because of its excellent hitting and defense.

According to Baseball Savant , the Cubs have a fielding run value of 70, which is significantly ahead of the second-place Toronto Blue Jays' total of 43. With players such as Pete Crow-Armstrong, Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner and Bregman leading the way, the defense has helped make up for some of the poor pitching.

As for the offense, the Cubs set a National League record for home runs in a month with 62 in August, which was more of the same for a team that leads the league in runs scored.

Crow-Armstrong has been the driving force of that offense with his combination of power and speed, which has resulted in 45 home runs and 40 stolen bases. He is the overwhelming favorite to take home the NL MVP and someone who could potentially swing a short playoff series now that Chicago has reached the postseason.

Bregman overcame a slow start to become one of the team's leading hitters, while Seiya Suzuki provided plenty of pop outside of the two big names.

Ultimately, the Cubs' pitching woes could prove too much to overcome in the playoffs, but the offense and defense will give them a chance in any series.

articles.title: Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong becomes seventh player in MLB history with a 40-40 season
articles.summary: The Cubs center fielder came into Thursday's game with 45 home runs and 39 stolen bases
articles.body:
Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh player in Major League Baseball history to achieve 40 home runs with 40 stolen bases in a single season during the Chicago Cubs' 2-1 win over the Miami Marlins on Thursday.

With the win, the Cubs also clinched a berth in the postseason with one of the National League's wild-card playoff bids.

Crow-Armstrong got on a base with a leadoff walk on seven pitches against Miami Marlins starter Tyler Phillips . He took off for the milestone steal on Phillips' first pitch to the next batter, Seiya Suzuki .

The Cubs center fielder finished the day batting 1-for-3.

Crow-Armstrong came into Thursday's matchup versus the Marlins with 45 home runs, tied for the MLB lead. He reached the 40-homer mark on Sept. 6 , also against the Marlins with Phillips pitching. At the time, he had 33 steals with 18 games remaining in the regular season.

That made Crow-Armstrong the first player in Cubs history to register 40 homers and 30 steals in a season. And at 24 years old, he joined José Canseco (1988) and Alex Rodriguez (1998) in reaching those numbers during a season at age 24 or younger. Canseco won American League MVP honors the year he had his 40-40 season.

Crow-Armstrong is a virtual certainly to join Canseco with an MVP award to go with his 40-40 achievement. In addition to his MLB-leading 45 homers, he ranks fourth with 107 RBI and fifth in stolen bases, while leading the National League with a .951 OPS.

Including Thursday's game, Crow-Armstrong has stolen a base in three of his past four contests. Only four more games were left on the schedule, but he can go into the Cubs' final series before the postseason (three games versus the Boston Red Sox ) without having to chase down that 40th steal.

Preceding Crow-Armstrong in the 40-40 club were Shohei Ohtani (who posted a 50-50 season in 2023), Ronald Acuña Jr. (41-73, 2024), Alfonso Soriano (46-41, 2006), Rodriguez (42-46), Barry Bonds (42-40, 1996) and Canseco (42-40).

In Cubs franchise history, the fourth-year star became the second player with a 30-30 campaign (joining Sammy Sosa), having now done it for two consecutive seasons. Crow-Armstrong is also the only player in team history to hit 30-plus doubles along with 30 homers and 30 steals.

Additionally, he has the most homers by a left-handed batter (topping Billy Williams' 42 in 1970), and the seventh with 45 or more homers in a single season. The other Cubs sluggers to hit 45 or more homers are Ernie Banks (twice), Hack Wilson, Andre Dawson, Dave Kingman, Sosa (five times) and Derrek Lee.

articles.title: What went wrong for the 2026 Seattle Mariners? And where do they go from here?
articles.summary: For Seattle, the vibes were off before Opening Day even arrived — and the Mariners never fully recovered.
articles.body:
Just 11 months ago, the Seattle Mariners were on the doorstep of the franchise's first World Series appearance. On Thursday, the Mariners were eliminated from playoff contention, the mathematical conclusion of a months-long march toward arguably the most disappointing finish for any MLB team in 2026.

Where to even begin? When a team triumphs, we hear refrains about how it takes everybody — from players to coaches to front office to ownership to behind-the-scenes personnel — to achieve something great. On the flip side, a letdown of this magnitude is also undoubtedly a group effort.

In 2026, catcher Cal Raleigh endured a historic regression from MVP candidate to a multi-month mega-slump that sank his season's statline beyond repair. Without an offensive anchor, the Seattle lineup never found momentum, withering into one of the league's weakest run-production outfits. A rotation that served as the backbone of the franchise's success over the past half-decade failed to provide a sturdy foundation, and for the first time in years, the bullpen was downright bad. Amplifying the pitching staff's shortcomings was a sloppy defense that ranked among MLB's worst by every available metric . Manager Dan Wilson, coming off one of the most confounding and widely criticized managerial maneuvers in recent postseason memory, did little to inspire confidence with his demeanor or in-game management. Heck, even the ballpark's newest statue celebrating franchise icon Ichiro Suzuki was dysfunctional .

Last October, the Mariners sojourned deeper into the postseason than ever before. Seattle arrived in the playoffs as AL West champions for the first time since 2001. They toppled the Detroit Tigers in the division series, advancing on a walk-off single from Jorge Polanco in the 15th inning of Game 5. A week later, the home crowd at T-Mobile Park enjoyed another epic moment when fan favorite Eugenio Suárez smacked a dramatic, go-ahead grand slam in ALCS Game 5 against the Blue Jays, putting Seattle one win away from the World Series.

But back in Toronto , the Blue Jays took Game 6. And in Game 7, eight outs away from their first trip to the Fall Classic, the Mariners fumbled as they approached the goal line. A 3-1 lead turned into a 4-3 deficit when George Springer flipped the script with a seismic, seventh-inning swing. The Mariners were unable to respond, and the Blue Jays were American League champions. The Mariners' wait persisted.

That Game 7 gut punch was a brutal blow for the organization. But once the sting of the loss subsided, it was clear the Mariners' October showing signaled positive momentum, on which the front office looked to capitalize. They re-signed first baseman Josh Naylor to a five-year, $92.5 million deal, by far the most lucrative free-agent contract handed out since Jerry Dipoto took over baseball operations after the 2015 season. Seattle bolstered the bullpen with the acquisition of hard-throwing lefty José Ferrer. They added Rob Refsnyder , a right-handed bat with an impeccable track record of mashing left-handed pitching. And to punctuate their offseason, the Mariners swung a trade with St. Louis to acquire Brendan Donovan , whose defensive versatility and stellar on-base skills fit perfectly on both sides of the ball.

The solid upgrades to the strong foundation already intact earned the Mariners the unfamiliar status of bona fide championship contenders from the moment they arrived in Arizona for spring training. Projection systems and oddsmakers pegged them as favorites to repeat as AL West champs, with FanGraphs giving Seattle the second-best World Series odds , behind only the Dodgers . It was a rare position for the franchise, but given the personnel, it felt deserved. At that point, it was on the team to embrace the high expectations and make the most of the opportunity.

Instead, the vibes were off before Opening Day even arrived. In the World Baseball Classic in March, Team Mexico outfielder Randy Arozarena attempted to greet Team USA catcher Raleigh with a handshake before an at-bat and got snubbed by his Mariners teammate. Just like that, two of Seattle's biggest names were making headlines for the wrong reasons. Raleigh was far from the only Team USA player to adopt an overly antagonistic attitude during the tournament, but his rejection of Arozarena attracted a wave of negative attention that felt foreign coming off a storybook 2025 that earned Raleigh the adoration and respect of both fans and fellow players.

Raleigh attempted to downplay the situation , but Arozarena was reportedly less forgiving . Still, it felt like a storyline that could've been laughed about in retrospect, had the Mariners played up to their potential. Instead, it became a strange cloud hanging over the first part of the season, all the more so as Arozarena surged to a career-best campaign while Raleigh slumped to an unthinkable degree. Of course, these were just two of the main characters in a comprehensive letdown involving so many others, but the moment made for an inauspicious start to the season.

Even so, it took a while for things to spiral beyond repair. For the first few months, several other teams with high hopes took turns in the spotlight as shamefully underperforming ballclubs. The Red Sox and Phillies fired their managers before the end of April. The Mets entered the season with the largest payroll in the league and played so poorly that they dismissed their skipper in June . The Tigers went 6-22 in May to doom their chances of chasing a World Series in Tarik Skubal's final season before free agency . The same Blue Jays that toppled the Mariners in the ALCS haven't been more than one game over .500 all season and will also miss October . (In case you're wondering: The last time both teams from a championship series failed to qualify for the postseason the following year was 2008, when neither the Rockies nor the Diamondbacks returned to October after clashing in the 2007 NLCS. The last time both ALCS teams finished the following season with a losing record was 1987 .)

But as this season wore on, Boston and Philadelphia were able to recover in time to secure postseason spots . The Tigers and Mets accepted their discouraging trajectories and offloaded major pieces at the trade deadline. The Mariners, meanwhile, treaded water in the mediocre American League (and even more mediocre AL West) for months before their fate started to crystallize.

Even as Seattle clumsily managed its crowded starting staff by oscillating between a six-man rotation and a so-called "piggyback" strategy, the team enjoyed an eight-game winning streak as the calendar flipped from May to June. A victory in Baltimore on June 9 earned them a three-game cushion atop the AL West. The rest of the month was a bit bumpier, but on July 5, the Mariners were 47-44 and still alone in first. At that point, FanGraphs pegged Seattle's chances of qualifying for October at 87.5%, with the third-highest World Series odds behind the Dodgers and Yankees .

This was remarkable considering how little they'd gotten from Raleigh, who missed a month due to an oblique strain that placed him on the IL for the first time in his career. And it wasn't just the missed time; Raleigh was hitting shockingly poorly both before and after his absence. Last season, Raleigh entered the All-Star break as the starting catcher for the American League and one of the biggest stories in baseball, with 38 home runs and a 1.011 OPS. This July, the Midsummer Classic went on without him, as Raleigh hit only nine home runs in 65 games before the break, with a .581 OPS.

Seattle making it that far into the season with minimal contributions from its best player could've been viewed as an opportunity for the team to really heat up if and when Raleigh started to look more like himself. And Raleigh did eventually find his footing — he ranks top-10 in MLB in fWAR and wRC+ since Aug. 16 — but by the time the star catcher reemerged, it was far too late, and the Mariners were too far out of the race.

Besides, Raleigh wasn't the only Mariner who notably underperformed at the plate. Julio Rodriguez , the other de facto face of the franchise, registered career lows in batting average, on-base percentage and slugging, making his latest power-speed milestone unusually unsatisfying. Naylor's slugging output has lagged far behind almost every other every-day first baseman , and his overly aggressive approach with minimal pop — only three qualified hitters have seen fewer pitches per plate appearance — made him more of a rally-killer than a run-producer. Top prospect Colt Emerson looked overmatched in his first taste of the majors, posting a .246 OBP across 241 plate appearances before he was shut down due to a wrist injury that the 20-year-old belatedly admitted had been bothering him for a while .

Outside of Arozarena's All-Star efforts and solid seasons from underrated slugger Dominic Canzone and 22-year-old second baseman Cole Young , silver linings in Seattle's lineup have been tough to identify. Scoring has been a chore for much of the season, as evidenced by top-line markers (28th in runs per game, 29th in OPS) as well as more subtle indicators of offensive ineptitude. The Mariners rank 30th in doubles with just 199, which has them on pace for their fewest in a full season in franchise history.

The Mariners lost eight of 10 to finish July five games below .500. But because the AL standings were so unintimidating — and because there was so much invested in this season for Seattle — the team was a buyer at the trade deadline, adding outfielder Taylor Ward from Baltimore and reliever Seranthony Dominguez from Chicago . These additions, though, did little to alter the troubling trajectory. Ward promptly plummeted into the worst slump of his career — he has quite literally the worst batting average in the league since the deadline — and Dominguez has hardly solved the bullpen woes.

Seattle then lost seven of eight after the trade deadline, including getting swept at home by the Rays , a resounding demonstration of how far the Mariners had fallen from the upper class of the league. A late comeback in Houston on Aug. 14 dissolved into another walk-off defeat against an Astros team that had surged back into first. Four days later in Milwaukee , the Mariners lost 22-0, the most lopsided loss in franchise history. The lowlight of that embarrassing showing was a total brain fart from Rodriguez, who forgot how many outs there were while trailing by 19 runs and tossed the ball into the stands, assuming an eternal eighth inning had finally ended.

While that Rodriguez gaffe came long after the game had been decided, the 25-year-old has had a few other, far more costly miscues in the outfield, including a massive blunder in Boston a few weeks later while protecting a one-run, ninth-inning lead that eventually lead to — you guessed it — a walk-off loss. These were just a few snapshots in a season in which Rodriguez showed huge regression as a defender, grading out as below average by most metrics after his glove rated as one of the best at his position across his first four seasons. Rodriguez's surprising step back contributed to a Mariners defense that not only ranks last in MLB in Outs Above Average by a wide margin but also currently has the lowest team OAA since Statcast began tracking the stat in 2016, at minus-56.

That porous defense did few favors for a pitching staff that struggled in its own right. Occasional gems from Seattle's homegrown starters came here and there, but on the whole, the rotation was inconsistent, too often serving up backbreaking homers and struggling mightily away from pitcher-friendly T-Mobile Park. And on the rare occasion when the starting pitcher and offense combined to conjure a late lead, the bullpen — both ill-equipped and often mismanaged by Wilson — regularly bungled the later frames, amassing an agonizing collection of walk-off defeats.

All of these issues compounded in the second half: Seattle's 5.15 ERA since the All-Star break is the fourth-highest mark in MLB behind only the A's, Rockies and Reds , and the Mariners have allowed a jaw-dropping 101 homers across those 61 games — 13 more than the next-highest total ( Colorado with 88).

In hindsight, an offseason that looked like a smash hit turned out to be a dud. Naylor took a sizable step in the wrong direction, making the four years and roughly $80 million remaining on his contract look rather onerous. Refsnyder was a disaster, hitting .140 across 114 at-bats before being released midseason. Donovan was reasonably productive when available, but injuries limited him to 39 games. Ferrer has been serviceable, but the hard-throwing lefty has not taken the step forward many hoped to see with his move from Washington to Seattle; his strikeout rate has actually dropped.

Add these disappointing additions to a group of holdovers who failed to elevate their games in arguably the most important season in recent Mariners history, and this team turned out to be not nearly good enough.

Since a series win over Toronto in early July, the Mariners are 27-40, the fourth-fewest wins in that span, ahead of only the Angels, A's and Rockies. Still, that cohort of bad ballclubs represented one final safety net in the schedule for the Mariners as they stumbled into September while still holding on in the underwhelming AL West and wild-card races. Seventeen of Seattle's final 22 games came against that aforementioned trio with the three worst records in the sport, offering the Mariners a final glimmer of hope.

But after Seattle played like a last-place team for much of July and August, it should've been no surprise that when those "favorable" matchups arrived, the Mariners slipped again. They dropped five of seven against the A's and two of three in Anaheim, clinching the franchise's first losing record since 2020. Another loss against the lowly Rockies followed this past weekend. And on Thursday, it was finally, officially over, as the Mariners were eliminated with the Rangers' 79th victory of the season .

The Mariners were actually eliminated from wild-card contention on Sunday, but it took four more days for them to be eliminated in the AL West race. That is a product of Texas ' and Houston's own poor showings atop the division. So if the totality of this Mariners team's disappointment weren't enough on its own, the fact that Seattle failed to take advantage of what could go down as the worst division in league history is the ultimate indictment of this catastrophe of a campaign.

This fall, the Mariners enter the offseason not with postseason heartbreak but with uncertainty all around.

How could one of the most promising seasons in franchise history disintegrate into such a disjointed mess? Can Raleigh and Rodriguez restore their status as unquestioned franchise cornerstones? Can the pitching staff regain its once-vaunted reputation? Wilson is reportedly not expected to return as manager, so who will be the skipper in 2027? Could there be more significant changes coming to the coaching staff? What should we make of Dipoto's front office, which has seemingly built a strong foundation but has reached the postseason only twice since taking over more than a decade ago? And assuming Dipoto and general manager Justin Hollander stay put, what moves will they be able to make before the expected lockout begins Dec. 1?

At the outset of 2026, few franchises looked to be trending more positively than the Seattle Mariners. As the season comes to a close, few teams face a wider range of questions that need to be answered.

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Says Cubs Are 'Built For the Weird S--t' After Clinching 2026 MLB Bracket Spot
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs clinched a playoff spot with Thursday's 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins, and Pete Crow-Armstrong believes the team's ability to handle adversity throughout the campaign could help in the postseason.
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs clinched a playoff spot with Thursday's 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins, and Pete Crow-Armstrong believes the team's ability to handle adversity throughout the campaign could help in the postseason.

"We're built for this weird s--t," he said, per Cubs insider Tony Andracki .

Much of the adversity Chicago has faced this season has come on the pitching side of things.

Ace Cade Horton was lost for the rest of the campaign in April because of Tommy John surgery, which was particularly difficult since fellow starting pitcher Justin Steele underwent the same surgery last season and is yet to pitch at the major league level in 2026.

What's more, Ben Brown was lost for the season with a neck injury while other pitchers such as Matthew Boyd and Edward Cabrera have been sidelined at times this year. The absence of Horton, Steele and Brown leaves the Cubs without arguably their best three starting options.

The injuries also became a problem in the bullpen with players such as Daniel Palencia, Phil Maton, Riley Martin and Hunter Harvey all hurt at times.

Fortunately for the Cubs, Crow-Armstrong and the rest of the offense has picked up the slack and actually leads the league in runs scored. Throw in a defense that is the best in baseball by a significant margin according to Baseball Savant's Fielding Run Value total , and the National League Central team was able to overcome the pitching concerns.

Still, there is more adversity hovering over the club with just three games remaining in the regular season.

Alex Bregman is dealing with multiple facial fractures after he was struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle, leaving his overall status uncertain heading into the playoffs. Bregman has been Chicago's second-best offensive player behind Crow-Armstrong since the All-Star break and likely needs to be in the lineup if the team is going to make a postseason run.

But Crow-Armstrong believes all that adversity will make the team stronger in the end, and he and his teammates will have a chance to prove it in the playoffs.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs clinch second straight MLB playoff berth with win over Marlins
articles.summary: The Cubs and White Sox punched their tickets to the postseason within minutes of each other on Thursday, marking just the fourth time both Chicago teams have...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs are officially heading back to the postseason. With a 2-1 win over the Miami Marlins on Thursday, the Cubs clinched a playoff spot for the second straight season.

The Cubs secured their postseason berth just minutes after their cross-town rivals, the Chicago White Sox , who are back in the playoffs after a five-year break and three 100-loss seasons.

It's just the fourth time in MLB history that both the Cubs and the White Sox have made the playoffs, with the pair both earning postseason berths in 1906, 2008, 2020 and now 2026, via MLB's Sarah Langs . Thursday marks the first time that both Chicago teams clinched on the same day.

Although Miami got on the board first with an RBI single in the third, Seiya Suzuki delivered with a solo homer in the fifth inning. An RBI single from Nico Hoerner in the sixth ended up being enough for the Cubs to pull off the win, with reliever Ryan Zeferjahn closing out the game with a hitless ninth.

During the game, star outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong continued his MVP campaign by stealing his 40th base of the season. That made him the seventh player in MLB history to achieve a 40/40 season .

After the game, Crow-Armstrong spoke about the Cubs rising above adversity to return to the playoffs.

"We're built for the weird s***," Crow-Armstrong said, via Cubs reporter Tony Andracki .

The Cubs' victory secures them a wild-card berth. The San Diego Padres and Philadelphia Phillies are also in line for wild-card berths, but the teams' close records mean they will likely be jockeying for the Nos. 4, 5 and 6 seeds through the final weekend of the season.

The Milwaukee Brewers clinched the National League Central earlier this month, leaving the Cubs to finish second in the division.

articles.title: Yankees, Orioles Make MLB Schedule Change With Nor'easter in Latest Weather Forecast
articles.summary: The schedule of the upcoming three-game series between the New York Yankees and Baltimore Orioles has been changed.
articles.body:
The schedule of the upcoming three-game series between the New York Yankees and Baltimore Orioles has been changed.

On Thursday, the Yankees announced that a Saturday clash with the Orioles was rescheduled and will be made up as the first contest of a single-admission doubleheader on Friday due to incoming "sustained inclement weather."

According to The Weather Channel , a multi-day nor'easter storm is expected to impact the New York City area through the weekend.

Rain and wind are expected on Saturday and Sunday in the Bronx, per The Weather Channel .

Friday: High of 73 degrees, Low of 59 degrees, 40 percent chance of rain at night

Saturday: High of 66 degrees, Low of 55 degrees, 90 percent chance of rain

Sunday: High of 65 degrees, Low of 59 degrees, 70 percent chance of rain

The updated schedule isn't a complete surprise, as Yankees manager Aaron Boone previously revealed that there were discussions surrounding a doubleheader between the two teams due to the weather forecast, per MLB.com's Bryan Hoch .

The series between the two American League East rivals doesn't carry any playoff implications, as the Orioles were eliminated from postseason contention on Thursday.

Meanwhile, New York is locked into the No. 1 AL Wild Card spot.

The Yankees were initially set to honor Hall of Famer CC Sabathia with a uniform number retirement and Monument Park plaque on Saturday, although the ceremony was also moved up to Friday. It will take place prior to the first game of the doubleheader.

The opening contest will start on Friday at 4:05 p.m. ET, while the second game begins no earlier than 7:05 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Braves place pitcher Martín Pérez on 15-day IL, sidelining him until NLDS
articles.summary: Atlanta likely won't need the veteran starter in the wild-card playoff round, but pitching depth will become an issue as the postseason progresses.
articles.body:
With three games remaining before the 2026 MLB postseason begins, the Atlanta Braves will be missing one of their starting pitchers through the first round of the playoffs.

Martín Pérez was placed on the 15-day injured list with low back inflammation, the Braves announced on Thursday . Atlanta was able to backdate Pérez's IL stint to Sept. 21, which means he will be eligible to return on Oct. 6. Game 3 of the National League Division Series is scheduled for that date .

Pérez felt discomfort in his back during Sunday's 4-2 win over the Houston Astros , according to Braves manager Walt Weiss . The left-hander pitched 4 1/3 innings, allowing 1 run and 6 hits with 2 strikeouts and 2 walks.

With a best-of-three format in the wild-card round, the Braves likely wouldn't have used Pérez as a starter. Perhaps he would have pitched in long relief. But Atlanta is expected to start Chris Sale and Tyler Mahle in the first two games of the wild-card series, with Grant Holmes getting the nod in Game 3, if necessary.

However, if the Braves make a deeper run into the playoffs, Pérez's absence could be an issue as postseason series get longer and pitching staffs get worn down. If he ends up returning by the NLDS, Atlanta will probably consider that an acceptable outcome.

Pérez signed a minor-league deal with the Braves in January before winning a rotation spot in spring training. In 26 starts (30 appearances), he has compiled a 3.09 ERA with 102 strikeouts and 65 walks in 142 innings. That is his highest innings total since 2022.

The staff doesn't have many other starting pitchers. Bryce Elder is on the IL after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his right knee and the hope is that he can return around the same time as Pérez. Reynaldo López is also sidelined with right shoulder inflammation with a possibility of returning later in the postseason.

If those options aren't eventually available, Atlanta will have to use JR Ritchie as a fourth starter. He has compiled a 4.79 ERA in 16 appearances (10 starts) with 66 strikeouts and 41 walks in 67 2/3 innings. Other possibilities are AJ Smith-Shawver (five starts this season, 6.43 ERA) or using multiple pitchers in bullpen games.

To take Pérez's place on the active roster, Elieser Hernández was recalled from Triple-A Gwinnett. In 25 appearances (12 starts), he has a 4.64 ERA with 77 strikeouts in 85 1/3 innings.

articles.title: Updated 2026 MLB Playoffs Bracket Picture and Standings After Guardians Clinch Berth
articles.summary: Another September surge has lifted the Cleveland Guardians to the MLB playoffs for the third consecutive season.
articles.body:
Another September surge has lifted the Cleveland Guardians to the MLB playoffs for the third consecutive season.

The Guardians clinched their postseason berth on Thursday with a 1-0 road win over the Boston Red Sox.

While not as dramatic as their historic 2025 comeback , the Guardians were five games under .500 (61-66) as recently as Aug. 19 after a 1-0 loss to the San Francisco Giants.

Since that date, though, the Guardians have gone 22-10 to put themselves back into the playoffs in the American League for the eighth time in the last 10 seasons.

If there is a reason to be optimistic about the Guardians having a deep playoff run, it's built around the top of their pitching staff. Rookie Parker Messick could finish in the top three of AL Cy Young voting. Gavin Williams has been up and down throughout the year, but his 244 strikeouts leads the AL. Cade Smith is the second-most valuable reliever in the AL by fWAR .

One reason for Cleveland's ascent up the standings was the front office surprisingly making bold swings prior to the trade deadline. Jo Adell, Nathaniel Lowe, Foster Griffin and Craig Yoho were all acquired on Aug. 3 to provide a boost.

Griffin and Yoho have struggled since coming over, but Adell and Lowe have provided some much-needed pop to the lineup with 11 combined homers.

The other primary offensive contributors leading to Cleveland making it back to the playoffs have been Chase DeLauter, Steven Kwan and Travis Bazzana. The impact from Kwan and Bazzana has largely been felt during the stretch run.

Kwan, in particular, has completely turned his season around after a disastrous first half when he hit .225/.332/.282 in 89 games. He has a .355/.440/.429 slash line and ranks seventh among all position players in fWAR since the All-Star break.

José Ramírez, who has been their stalwart for the past 10 years, struggled this season in part due to a hamate bone injury that required surgery in June. He has started to hit better lately and will be a huge piece if the team is going to make a run in October.

This lineup still doesn't boast a lot of power that is often required to win in October, but the group of DeLauter, Kwan, Bazzana, Adell and Ramírez can be good enough that the Guardians surprise people as the franchise seeks to win its first World Series title since 1948.

articles.title: Brewers win 100 games for first time in franchise history, topping last season's previous high of 97 victories
articles.summary: Milwaukee has won 90 or more games in four consecutive seasons and five of the past six.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers won their 100th game in a season for the first time in franchise history with Thursday's 5-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park.

The triple-digit win total tops the organization's previous mark for most wins in a season, set with last year's 97-65 record. Prior to that franchise high, Milwaukee posted 96 wins during the 2018 and 2011 campaigns. The Brewers have won 90 or more games in five of the past six seasons.

At 100-59, Milwaukee has the best record in Major League Baseball and still has an opportunity to clinch the top seed and home field advantage throughout the postseason.

Milwaukee took a 1-0 lead in the second inning on an RBI double from Sal Frelick . With the score tied at 1-1 in the eighth, the Brewers went back ahead on run-scoring singles by Jake Bauers , Cooper Pratt and Joey Ortiz . Jackson Chourio put the Brewers up 5-1 with his 25th home run of the season, a solo shot in the ninth off Tim Mayza .

Opener Shane Drohan allowed Philadelphia's only one run in the third inning on a double by Kyle Schwarber and a run-scoring single from Bryce Harper . After Drohan's 2 2/3 innings, four other Brewers pitchers threw 6 1/3 scoreless innings, led by Aaron Ashby 's two perfect frames.

Before getting to 100 wins on Thursday, Milwaukee was one of seven MLB teams that had never reached that threshold. Now, the Brewers have separated themselves from the Toronto Blue Jays , San Diego Padres , Texas Rangers , Washington Nationals , Miami Marlins and Colorado Rockies .

Despite winning 100 games, the Brewers haven't had a winning streak of more than five games this season, as pointed out by MLB.com's Adam McCalvy . They put together three different five-game streaks this season, but never got to a sixth consecutive win.

That will continue even if Milwaukee sweeps its final three regular-season games versus the St. Louis Cardinals . The Brewers lost to the Phillies on Tuesday, 6-4 .

Also making the Brewers' win total impressive is that they had a losing record during their first full month of the season, going 12-13 in April. They were 16-14 going into May, when the team shifted into another gear with a 19-7 month. Since the All-Star break, Milwaukee has a 41-22 record (a .650 winning percentage).

This story will be updated with more information.

articles.title: Astros rookie Lucas Spence hits his first 3 career homers in the same game
articles.summary: Spence is the third player in MLB history to do that.
articles.body:
A first career homer is an unforgettable moment for an MLB rookie. Lucas Spence tripled that magic on Thursday, to the benefit of the Houston Astros .

Facing the Athletics in West Sacramento, the 23-year-old center fielder hit his first career homer in the second inning, his second career homer in the seventh inning and his third career homer in the ninth inning. The Astros won 7-5, allowing them to stay tied atop the AL West with the Texas Rangers .

The three homers came at the Athletics' temporary home of Sutter Health Park in front of a crowd of 9,367.

MLB Pipeline currently ranks Spence as the No. 12 prospect in the Astros organization. Most of his stock comes via his glove in center field, his speed on the basepaths and his patience at the plate. His power is actually ranked as his worst tool, backed up by a career .402 slugging percentage in the minors.

Spence made his MLB debut in July, was optioned a couple of weeks later and was called back up on Wednesday. Entering Thursday, he was 6-for-40 in his MLB career, with one double, 17 strikeouts and a .419 OPS. That works out to seven total bases in 15 games.

Then he posted 12 total bases in a single game.

According to MLB.com's Sarah Langs , Spence is only the third player in MLB history to hit his first three career homers in the same game. The first was Chicago White Sox catcher Seby Zavala on July 31, 2021. The second was St. Louis Cardinals outfielder Joshua Baez on Aug. 15 of this season.

Spence's homers, however, came at a huge moment for the Astros. Had Houston scored three fewer runs, they would be down a game behind the Rangers as both teams enter their final three games of the season. Instead, they're still tied, which is effectively a lead because the Astros own the tiebreaker.

The rest of the Astros' schedule is against the A's, while the Rangers will begin a three-game road series against the Minnesota Twins on Friday. We'll see if Spence is any higher than eighth in the lineup for those remaining games.

articles.summary: Even in a season when Aaron Judge missed significant time due to injury and several other high-profile stars also had abbreviated years, the outfield still featured some of baseball's brightest stars.
articles.body:
Even in a season when Aaron Judge missed significant time due to injury and several other high-profile stars also had abbreviated years, the outfield still featured some of baseball's brightest stars.

Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is putting the finishing touches on what is expected to be an NL MVP season, while San Diego Padres star Fernando Tatis Jr. has put a quiet first half far in the rearview with a huge second half.

There has also been an influx of talent at the position, with rookies Chase DeLauter, Carson Benge and Tristan Peters all making an immediate impact, while former top prospects Jordan Walker and Jac Caglianone have also enjoyed breakout seasons.

We've ranked the top 25 outfielders of the 2026 season, focusing solely on this year's production while ignoring past track record and future projections. Offensive and defensive contributions were both part of the conversation. While each player's WAR is included, this is not simply a WAR leaderboard.

Acuña won 2025 NL Comeback Player of the Year with a 161 OPS+ and 3.1 WAR in 95 games in his return from a torn ACL, but a nagging hamstring issue has led to a less dynamic follow-up campaign. The 28-year-old has been a 20/20 player over 104 games, but his .259/.352/.462 line and 1.8 WAR left him short of cracking the top 25.

The Blue Jays acquired Bateman in the deal that sent Kevin Gausman to the Cubs. He immediately plugged him in as their starting center fielder after also moving Daulton Varsho at the deadline. The 24-year-old made his MLB debut on Aug. 7. He is hitting .320/.394/.413 with a 124 OPS+ in 172 plate appearances. It's too small a sample to earn a top-25 spot, but impressive enough for a mention.

When healthy, Judge has been plenty productive, posting a 141 OPS+ with 18 home runs and 41 RBI, but with only 66 games played this season, he has simply not been one of the 25 best outfielders in the 2026 season. The Yankees have weathered the storm without him for the most part, but his postseason status will be a major story.

With a .273/.329/.553 line since the All-Star break that includes 16 extra-base hits, nine home runs and 19 RBI, Mesa has given a first-place Tampa Bay squad another highly productive bat as they push toward October. Prospect followers might remember him as the younger brother of the more hyped Victor Victor Mesa, who both signed with the Marlins in 2018.

Simpson is hitting .309 with 174 hits and 46 steals, making him one of the more dynamic table-setters in the league at a time when players with his skill set have become few and far between. He has strong defensive metrics in left field (9 DRS, 8 OAA), but his .359 slugging percentage and 96 OPS+ ultimately capped his impact enough to land him just outside the top 25.

A recurring hip issue that eventually led to season-ending surgery earlier this month limited Buxton to 93 games this season, but he still logged the seventh 3-WAR campaign of his career. His 129 OPS+ ranks 10th among outfielders with at least 400 plate appearances.

A calf strain has limited Soto to 107 games and 463 plate appearances in 2026. Otherwise, his 157 OPS+ would tie Pete Crow-Armstrong for the National League lead. He has again tallied more walks (76) than strikeouts (64). His .394 on-base percentage is again among the best in baseball.

After posting a .157 batting average and 47 OPS+ in 232 plate appearances as a rookie, Caglianone has quickly started delivering on the huge offensive upside that helped him fly through the minors after going No. 6 overall in the 2024 draft. The 23-year-old is hitting .322/.361/.528 over 191 plate appearances since the All-Star break.

Mitchell played just 113 games over the previous three seasons while navigating a variety of injuries, but he has finally stayed healthy this year. He will likely never be a plus defender, but his defensive metrics were a less significant drain on his value this season than in past years.

Injuries limited Trout to 111 games in 2023 and 2024. During a relatively healthy 2025 campaign, he posted a career-low .797 OPS with 1.7 WAR in 130 games. With improvements to his walk rate (12.3 to 16.2 percent) and strikeout rate (32.1 to 28.9 percent), Wood has continued his development as a hitter this season while logging a second straight 30-homer campaign. Poor defense and a second-half swoon (35 G, .628 OPS, 2 HR) keep him from cracking the top 10, but he remains one of the game's brightest young stars just days removed from his 24th birthday.

That's it, end of list. Alex Rodriguez, Mike Trout, Julio Rodríguez, Andruw Jones, César Cedeño and Vada Pinson did it twice. Barry Bonds, Carlos Beltrán and several others did it once. No one has ever done it three times at that age.

Beyond just the raw counting numbers, he also raised his on-base percentage from .308 to .342 and posted substantially better defensive metrics. As good as he already is, it's reasonable to believe he still hasn't reached his ceiling.

Michael Harris II has quietly piled up 18.9 WAR over his first five seasons in the big leagues, thanks to a healthy mix of power, speed and standout defense in center field.

There have been ups and downs along the way, but his 4.8 WAR this season is his highest since he won the 2022 NL Rookie of the Year honors. His 26 home runs are a career high.

A 3.8 percent walk rate and .317 on-base percentage remain limiting factors to his overall offensive value, but his well-rounded impact has been on full display during a standout 2026 campaign.

A year ago, Seiya Suzuki served as the Cubs' primary designated hitter after being viewed as the weak link in an outfield logjam featuring Ian Happ, Pete Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Tucker.

This year, he has provided Gold Glove-caliber defense in right field and continued to serve as one of the primary run producers in the middle of the highest-scoring offense in baseball.

The 32-year-old will be a free agent this winter. In a market relatively thin on impact bats, the Cubs will no doubt have some competition to re-sign him while also navigating Ian Happ's free agency.

Andy Pages broke through with a 114 OPS+ and 27 home runs during the 2025 season. He solidified his status as the Dodgers' everyday center fielder in 2026 while earning his first All-Star selection.

articles.summary: October is almost upon us, meaning the MLB's best will soon lock horns as part of a 12-team fight for World Series glory.
articles.body:
October is almost upon us, meaning the MLB's best will soon lock horns as part of a 12-team fight for World Series glory.

Something else is just around the corner, too: the ignition of the hot stove's burners.

Free agency is fast approaching, and it's carrying even more uncertainty than normal given all of the unknowns with the collective bargaining agreement negotiations. It's also featuring some bright stars and proven support players, both of which are featured in this latest rumor roundup.

This can't be a comfortable time for many MLB free agents, but Arozarena seems an obvious exception.

A strong season at the plate—perhaps the strongest of his career—has Arozarena poised to snag a big paycheck on the open market. His 109 runs are already a personal-best, and all three layers of his .279/.380/.479 slash line sit higher than he's ever posted over a full season.

The money is almost certainly coming, it's just a matter of where from. And it seems Arozarena has a preference on that. According to Ryan Divish of the Seattle Times , Arozarena is "going to" leave Seattle and "would probably prefer to stay on the East Coast."

Arozarena, who has tallied at least 20 homers and 20 steals in six consecutive campaigns, would be a great for any offense-seeking shopper. The Atlanta Braves, in particular, might be all the way in given the boxes he'd check as a powerful (and speedy) hitter from the right side and capable corner outfielder.

Prediction: Arozarena signs with Atlanta.

Big Contract, Retirement Both Possibilities for Sonny Gray?

It's possible that with every strikeout, inning completed and win secured this offseason, Gray could hear a cash register's ring in his head. But will that be enough to drown out the siren's song of retirement?

It sounds like everything is on the table for the 36-year-old. Per Mass Live's Chris Cotillo , Gray could fetch a similar deal to the three-year, $75 million deal Nathan Eovaldi inked with the Texas Rangers two years back. But Cotillo also noted that Gray relayed in a recent interview with The Boston Globe he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family indicated any desire for him to do so.

Only Gray knows what he's thinking, and since he doesn't need to make a decision right now, it's very possible even if he isn't sure. If he wants to keep playing, though, he has clearly set himself up to strike it rich in free agency. He is tied for the MLB lead with 18 wins (against only five losses) and owns a 2.72 ERA over his 169 innings pitched.

Maybe this is an attempt to wish something into existence, but our crystal ball sees Gray keeping his career going. He could probably handpick his landing spot after a season this strong, but why bother tinkering with what's obviously working so well?

Prediction: Gray re-signs with the Red Sox.

A $500 Million Contract Coming for Tarik Skubal?

There might be a million different scenarios for how this offseason plays out. And every last one of them happens to involve Skubal signing a massive—very possibly record-setting—contract.

ESPN's Jeff Passan explained: "The [contract] number will be huge. Bear in mind that Skubal turns 30 in November and never before has a pitcher age 30 or older received more than Stephen Strasburg's $245 million (on a seven-year deal) in free agency. Provided there is no salary cap, Skubal could get double that."

Skubal was the AL Cy Young winner each of the past two seasons. He has been nearly as dominant during this campaign despite dealing with both an elbow procedure and a midseason relocation (from Detroit to the L.A.). His ERA sits south of 3.00, and he's averaging more than 10 strikeouts and fewer than two walks per nine innings pitched.

His contract number will be enormous, which might restrict his list of landing spots to the deepest-pocketed clubs in the biggest markets. This is almost assuredly a cannonball splash the New York Mets would love to make, but it's hard to imagine the Los Angeles Dodgers letting him get away.

Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers.

articles.summary: The MLB regular season is approaching its end, but the real excitement is just beginning.
articles.body:
The MLB regular season is approaching its end, but the real excitement is just beginning.

All four divisional races in the National League have been settled. However, the wild card race is intensifying. The Padres and Cubs have both clinched wild card spots, though they will be vying for positioning. Meanwhile, the Phillies lead the Diamondbacks by two games for the third NL wild card spot.

In the American League, the wild card race is all settled, but there is still some drama as the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are tied atop the AL West, with the Astros in front courtesy of a tie-breaker. Meanwhile, the AL Central sees the Guardians and White Sox going head-to-head for the division title, though both are assured at least the third wild card berth.

After a look at the updated standings, we'll break down our predictions for how the 2026 postseason might play out.

*x-clinched division; y-clinched wild card; e-eliminated from playoff contention

*y-clinched wild card; z-clinched playoff berth

The greatest rivalry in baseball is likely to return as the Yankees and Red Sox look poised to face off in the AL Wild Card Series for the second consecutive year. The Yankees are still chasing their first World Series title since 2009, while the Red Sox's postseason appearance is especially impressive after an inconsistent season.

As recently as June 24, the Red Sox sat 14 games below .500 with a 32–46 record. Boston is just the fourth team ever to reach the playoffs after being at least 14 games under .500, and their 75-game start (31–44) is the worst for any playoff team in MLB history. Their turnaround has been dramatic, but September has been tough; the Sox rank last in runs per game (3.00).

The biggest question is whether Aaron Judge will return. Regardless, the Yankees have home-field advantage and a strong pitching staff, with Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, and Max Fried likely starting in this best-of-three series. With their depth and momentum, I predict the Yankees will advance past Boston again.

Meanwhile, either the Astros or Rangers will host the Guardians or White Sox in the other wild card matchup. I expect the Astros to win the division and defeat the White Sox, relying on playoff experience and clutch play from Jose Altuve and Yordan Alvarez.

This would set up an ALDS between the Guardians and Astros, where the Guardians' pitching trio—Foster Griffin, Parker Messick, and Gavin Williams—could get them to the ALCS, especially with Steven Kwan's hot streak.

In the other ALDS, the Yankees would face the Rays, who feature a dominant rotation and lineup depth. With Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez, and Freddy Peralta now all in top form, I give the edge to the Rays.

This sets up a Rays-Guardians ALCS, where the Rays' versatility gets them back to the World Series.

The burning question on everyone's mind: Will the Dodgers win the pennant again? We'll get to that soon.

It looks like the NL Wild Card Series could feature a rematch between the Padres and Cubs for the second straight year. This time, the Padres have home-field advantage. While the Cubs lead MLB in runs per game, the Padres have been red-hot, winning 16 of their last 20 games. Fernando Tatis Jr. and Jackson Merrill have been outstanding since the All-Star break, and Manny Machado is returning to form. In addition, Nick Pivetta is back in the rotation, giving the Padres even more depth.

In the other Wild Card series, the Braves are projected to face the Phillies in an NL East showdown. The Braves feature MVP-caliber talents like Matt Olson and Ronald Acuna Jr., but their postseason hopes depend heavily on pitching. The Phillies counter with an impressive trio in Cristopher Sanchez, Zack Wheeler, and Jesus Luzardo.

Looking ahead to the NLDS, the Padres would meet the Brewers. Milwaukee secured the top seed and is celebrating its first-ever 100-win season. Although the Brewers are not known for their power, their pitching staff, led by likely Cy Young winner Jacob Misioroski and Logan Henderson, should give them an early advantage and a path to the NLCS.

Meanwhile, I expect the Dodgers to take on the Phillies again in the NLDS. The Phillies may be looking for revenge, but the Dodgers' lineup, with stars like Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, and Teoscar Hernandez, along with a hall-of-fame-like rotation, make them tough to beat.

This all sets up an NLCS clash between the Dodgers and Brewers. Milwaukee, who were swept by Los Angeles last year, should be more competitive this time. However, the Brewers' lack of power will cost them yet again, and the Dodgers seem poised for another trip to the World Series.
