articles.body: Carlos Rodon’s latest philanthropic honor is very much tied to one of the most personal chapters of his life outside of baseball. The New York Yankees pitcher and his wife, Ashley Rodon, suffered two miscarriages before welcoming their daughter Willow and raising a family of three children. That experience became the launching pad for a nonprofit that helps other families who are experiencing infertility and pregnancy loss.The Players Trust announced Rodon as the season’s final Most Valuable Philanthropist honoree on September 23, 2026. In addition to the recognition, The Players Trust also presented a $10,000 grant to the Carlos Rodon Foundation, which will offer the organization additional funding to help families dealing with financial struggles connected to fertility issues.MLB star Carlos Rodon earns Players Trust honor for foundationThe Players Trust named Carlos Rodon its Most Valuable Philanthropist for September, an award that honors MLB players for their charitable work and impact on their community outside of the game of baseball. The September award is the last of its kind for the 2026 season and comes with a $10,000 grant to the charity of the recipient’s choice.Rodon’s money will be directed to the Carlos Rodon Foundation, the nonprofit he and his wife Ashley Rodon created. The organization seeks to help couples and families struggling with infertility and pregnancy loss, especially by reducing some of the financial barriers associated with fertility treatment.Rodon’s dedication to the cause is linked to his own family’s experience, the Players Trust said. The program is designed to assist eligible families with infertility following pregnancy loss who are seeking fertility treatment, including IVF. The foundation says its bigger mission is to help families find treatment and resources while lowering the financial burden that comes with growing a family.That work has become much larger in scale. articles.title: Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge, Pete Crow-Armstrong Among Top-Selling Jerseys of 2026 MLB Season
articles.summary: Superstar sluggers Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge and Pete Crow-Armstrong top the list of the players with the highest-selling jerseys for the 2026 MLB season.
articles.body:
Superstar sluggers Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge and Pete Crow-Armstrong top the list of the players with the highest-selling jerseys for the 2026 MLB season.

Talkin' Baseball revealed the entire top 20 on Friday, and the names at the top didn't come as much of a surprise:

B/R's Undisputed MLB Outfielder Rankings 🔢

Ohtani has won an MVP award each of the past three seasons, including National League MVP in each of his first two campaigns with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Injuries have played a role in him failing to reach the offensive production he achieved in 2024 and 2025, though, when he smashed 54 and 55 home runs, respectively.

Still, despite being limited to 132 games, Ohtani is slashing .278/.381/.521 with 30 homers, 81 RBI and 89 runs scored.

Ohtani was also on pace for the best pitching season of his career, going 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts, but he has not pitched since July 3 because of injuries.

Judge has had an even more injury-plagued 2026 season with a fractured rib and calf strain limiting him to 66 games.

On the heels of winning back-to-back American League MVP awards, Judge is slashing just .241/.360/.511 with 18 homers and 41 RBI, and his status for the playoffs is uncertain after landing back on the injured list with a calf issue last week.

The 24-year-old Crow-Armstrong is enjoying a career year, and all signs point toward him being the man to beat for NL MVP honors.

PCA leads the NL in home runs (45), runs scored (119), slugging percentage (.575) and OPS (.949), plus he is hitting .280 with 107 RBI and 40 stolen bases for a Cubs team that is back in the playoffs for a second straight year.

Elsewhere on the jersey list, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and Yoshinobu Yamamoto combine with Ohtani to give the Dodgers an MLB-high four players in the top 20.

Meanwhile, Chicago White Sox rookie slugger Munetaka Murakami rounds out the list as a new entry at No. 20 with his 33 homers helping the White Sox return to the postseason for the first time since 2021.

articles.title: MLB wild card series set to begin days after 2026 regular season finale
articles.summary: Piter2121/Depositphotos MLB’s playoff picture comes into focus as the season winds down The 2026 MLB regular season ends Sunday, September 27, with the AL Ce...
articles.body:
MLB's playoff picture comes into focus as the season winds down

The 2026 MLB regular season ends Sunday, September 27, with the AL Central, AL West and final NL wild-card berth still to be decided. Several postseason seeds and wild-card matchups also remain unsettled.

Texas and Houston are tied atop the AL West, while Cleveland leads the White Sox by one game in the AL Central. Philadelphia holds the last NL wild-card position, two games ahead of Arizona .

Rangers and Astros are tied in the AL West

The Texas Rangers and Houston Astros are tied at 79-80 atop the AL West with three games remaining for each club. Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker, so Texas must finish with a better record to win the division.

Texas is three games behind the White Sox in the wild-card standings, making the division race its route to the postseason.

Guardians lead the White Sox in the AL Central

The Cleveland Guardians lead the AL Central at 83-76, one game ahead of the 82-77 Chicago White Sox. Both teams have clinched postseason berths, but the division title remains undecided.

Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland. If the teams finish with identical records, the White Sox will win the division.

Yankees and Red Sox have all but clinched AL wild card berths

The New York Yankees have secured the AL's top wild-card seed. The Boston Red Sox have also clinched a wild-card berth and currently hold the second position.

The White Sox have clinched a postseason berth but could still win the AL Central. Texas is three games behind Chicago in the wild-card standings, while Baltimore is four games back.

Padres and Cubs clinch as Phillies defend final wild-card spot

San Diego and Chicago have clinched NL wild-card berths, while Philadelphia holds the final spot without having secured it. Their current records are 89-70, 88-71 and 87-72, respectively.

The Padres lead the Cubs by one game and the Phillies by two. Arizona is 85-74, two games behind Philadelphia, and remains in contention for the final berth.

Rays , Braves, Brewers and Dodgers have already clinched division titles

The Tampa Bay Rays have clinched the AL East and the league's No. 1 seed. Atlanta has won the NL East, Milwaukee the NL Central and Los Angeles the NL West.

Milwaukee leads MLB at 100-59, while the Dodgers are 97-62. Both have secured first-round byes: the Brewers as the NL's No. 1 seed and the Dodgers as its No. 2 seed. Atlanta is locked into the NL's No. 3 seed and will play in the Wild Card Series.

How the 2026 MLB playoff bracket is shaping up

he top two division winners in each league advance directly to the Division Series. Tampa Bay has secured the AL's No. 1 seed, while the second AL bye remains tied to the unresolved Central and West races. Milwaukee and Los Angeles have secured the NL's two byes.

In each league's best-of-three Wild Card Series, the No. 3 seed hosts No. 6 and No. 4 hosts No. 5. The No. 3-versus-No. 6 winner then faces No. 2; the No. 4-versus-No. 5 winner faces No. 1.

Fun fact: The Yankees' 27 World Series titles are more than double the total of the next-closest club, the Cardinals , who have won 11, according to MLB's official postseason history.

Inside the American League's wild card matchups

If the current standings hold, the No. 6 White Sox would visit the No. 3 Astros. The winner would advance to face the AL's No. 2 seed. Chicago can still win the Central, and Houston is tied with Texas atop the West, so that matchup is not settled.

The No. 4 Yankees have clinched home field for their Wild Card Series. Boston currently occupies No. 5 and would visit New York if it retains that seed. The winner of the No. 4-versus-No. 5 series will face the top-seeded Rays.

Fun fact: The first World Series night game was played on October 13, 1971 . The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Baltimore Orioles 4–3 in Game 4.

A look at the National League's wild card pairings

Atlanta has secured the NL's No. 3 seed and will host the No. 6 seed. Philadelphia currently holds that position, but Arizona remains two games behind in the race for the final berth. The winner of that Wild Card Series will face the No. 2 Dodgers.

San Diego currently holds No. 4, one game ahead of the No. 5 Cubs. If those positions hold, the Padres will host Chicago, and the winner will face the top-seeded Brewers.

Regular season wraps up Sunday with wild card action starting Tuesday

The 2026 MLB regular season concludes Sunday, September 27. The best-of-three Wild Card Series begin Tuesday, September 29, with the postseason opening before October.

A lower seed can advance by winning two road games. The higher seed hosts every game in each Wild Card Series, whether it is a division winner or a wild-card team.

Dodgers eye a third title in five years as October nears

The Los Angeles Dodgers won the World Series in 2024 and 2025. They have clinched the NL West and the NL's No. 2 seed, earning a bye to the Division Series. Their current record is 97-62.

Another championship would give Los Angeles three consecutive World Series titles. Its first postseason opponent will be the winner of Atlanta's Wild Card Series against the NL's eventual No. 6 seed; Philadelphia currently holds that position.

Diamondbacks chase final NL berth as Orioles are eliminated

Arizona remains in contention for the NL's final wild-card berth. The Diamondbacks are 85-74, two games behind the 87-72 Phillies with three games remaining for each team.

Baltimore is 78-81 and four games behind the White Sox in the AL wild-card standings. With only three games left, the Orioles cannot catch Chicago and are out of the postseason race.

What's left to decide before the 2026 postseason begins

The AL Central and AL West titles remain undecided, and Philadelphia and Arizona are competing for the final NL wild-card berth. The White Sox have already clinched a postseason spot but can still win their division. Texas remains tied with Houston in the AL West.

The regular season concludes September 27. Once the remaining berths and seeds are decided, the Wild Card Series will determine which four winners advance to the Division Series.

The Dodgers enter this postseason as back-to-back champions, but their long-term roster is already a hot topic. Wondering what's next for Shohei Ohtani in Los Angeles? Check out this insider's bold prediction about his 2027 future.

October baseball is almost here and anything can happen

The 2026 postseason field will be set within a week, capping a wild card round loaded with pressure. Division winners Tampa Bay, Atlanta, Milwaukee and Los Angeles wait to see their opponents.

Every game left on the schedule now carries postseason weight for teams chasing October. Which team do you think will make the deepest run this year? Like this post and comment below.

articles.title: Yankees vs. Red Sox AL Wild Card Series Pick, Stat Predictions for Cam Schlittler, More Stars
articles.summary: At the end of play on August 1, the Tampa Bay Rays had the best record in the American League, the New York Yankees had the second-best record and the Boston Red Sox had the third-best record.
articles.body:
At the end of play on August 1, the Tampa Bay Rays had the best record in the American League, the New York Yankees had the second-best record and the Boston Red Sox had the third-best record.

Every single morning since then has been the same story: the inevitability of a Yankees-Red Sox wild card round rematch. It finally reached its crescendo on Friday afternoon, with Boston locking up the No. 5 seed after a 4-3 win over the Chicago Cubs on Friday.

It'll be the seventh time these teams have clashed in the postseason since 1999, each winning three of the previous series.

B/R's Undisputed MLB Outfielder Rankings 🔢

Who prevails in the rubber match of this decades-long, best-of-seven rivalry?

Simply put, the Yankees have the best pitching staff in baseball.

Even though Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón combined to miss about 40 starts, New York has allowed fewer runs than any other team this season. And now that the Yankees have had the full complement of that trio and Cam Schlittler available together for nearly a month, this rotation has become a terror.

It's not just the starters, either. The bullpen big three of David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, and Brent Headrick have been unflappable since the beginning of June, with a combined ERA of 1.46 in 154.1 innings of work.

Granted, October experience among those three is quite limited. We're talking six innings for Bednar, 1.1 for Blackburn and a goose egg for Headrick, so we'll see what happens in the ultimate pressure cooker. But they've played a massive role in the Yankees eclipsing 90 wins.

Meanwhile, the Boston team that destroyed everything in its path from late June through early August? Nowhere to be found lately, at 22-23 in its last 45 contests and averaging 3.8 runs per game.

Throw in home-field advantage and both Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger heating back up in a huge way over the past month and it's not at all difficult to envision the Yankees advancing from this matchup for a second consecutive year.

While the Yankees have allowed the fewest runs this season, the Red Sox are close behind at 3.8 runs allowed per game—their lowest mark since the Year of the Pitcher in 1968.

We shall see how they decide to line up Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Peyton Tolle for this series, but that's a trifecta that can hold its own against Schlittler and Co.

Provided Aroldis Chapman's recent lat soreness doesn't resurface next week, the one-two punch with Garrett Whitlock has been a late-inning tour de force. Garrett Crochet might be in the bullpen mix , too? And Brayan Bello is one heck of a bulk relief option, boasting a 2.28 ERA since the beginning of July.

Trevor Story has hit the ball well since returning from the IL in late August. Roman Anthony returned the same day (8/30) and has made a positive impact at the top of the lineup. If they can get Ceddanne Rafaela back to normal after his recent leg muscle strains, this offense should be able to scratch out at least a few runs in what is likely to be a series of pitching duels.

The three-time MVP-sized unknown in this series is Aaron Judge's availability for the Yankees.

Will they even have him on their wild card roster with his calf injury? Per MLB.com's Bryan Hoch , Aaron Boone said Tuesday, "We're planning on him not being a part of that (the wild card series)."

Judge had other thoughts the following day, saying he plans to play in Game 1.

Could he play right field if he makes it back, though?

If he can only DH, does that mean Ben Rice plays first base for just the second time since the trade deadline, while Luis García Jr. slides over to second base for the first time since last season?

Or do they save Judge for a pivotal pinch-hitting situation in each game—even though he has gone 2-for-27 with no extra-base hits and 17 strikeouts as a sub in his MLB career?

Basically, how much of a distraction is it going to cause if he's on the roster? And if he's not, how badly will New York miss a guy who's hit .355 with two home runs in eight career postseason games against the Red Sox?

Cam Schlittler, RHP, NYY: 7.0 IP, 4 H, 1 ER, 10 K

Not only is Schlittler going to win the AL Cy Young with his 1.95 ERA, but he has particularly owned Boston in his brief career. The ace from Massachusetts has made five starts against the Red Sox, allowing just two earned runs in 32.1 innings, for a 0.56 ERA. Maybe that changes on Tuesday, but he has shown no signs whatsoever of running out of gas as he approaches 200 innings pitched this season.

Payton Tolle, LHP, BOS: 5.1 IP, 5 H, 2 ER, 8 K

While Schlittler has dominated the Red Sox, Tolle has returned the favor to the Yankees. Granted, it's only two starts instead of five, but he has a 0.69 ERA, 0.54 WHIP and 12.5 K/9 against them. And with Tolle blossoming into a cult hero this season, it's almost inevitable that he is going to play a key role in this series.

Ben Rice, DH, NYY: 3-for-12, 1 HR, 3 RBI

Rice got the party started last year with a two-run home run off Bello in the first inning of Game 1. And if the Red Sox deploy Gray in Game 1, Rice just might hit a leadoff homer this year. Though he has a woeful .473 OPS against Boston in 2026, he has a 1.841 OPS in nine career plate appearances against Gray.

Willson Contreras, 1B, BOS: 1-for-12, 1 RBI, 6 K

This is the series' X-factor. Contreras has been Boston's most important bat with a .905 OPS. No one else on Boston who ranks top 12 in plate appearances can boast a better mark than .781.

But in addition to missing the past week with a knuckle injury, in 59 career plate appearances against the collection of Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón and David Bednar, he has gone 7-for-55 (.127 AVG) with one home run, four walks and 25 strikeouts—and the home run came off Rodón (Who maybe doesn't pitch in this series?) in 2017. If he keeps struggling against those arms, where does Boston's offense come from?

Curiously enough, New York's left-handed heavy lineup has actually fared pretty well against southpaws since Judge first hit the shelf at the end of May—which could prove pivotal against a disproportionately left-handed Red Sox pitching staff. (Spencer Jones, in particular, has been a reverse-splits unicorn with a 1.155 OPS against lefties this season.)

For how long we've been anticipating this wild card matchup, here's hoping it goes the distance. But the Yankees prevail, setting up a colossal showdown with Tampa Bay and yet another postseason series preview riddled with Judge-centric questions.
